acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of pitch attitude control
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Departure from controlled flight; loss of the aircraft.
acFhaData.effCrew: Unable to arrest flight-path divergence.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
acFhaData.effAc: Large excursions near the ground with a long, flexible fuselage.
acFhaData.effCrew: High workload; opposite-sense correction required.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of roll attitude control
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Departure from controlled flight.
acFhaData.effCrew: Unable to arrest bank divergence on an 80 m span.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of yaw and sideslip control
acFhaData.effAc: Uncontrollable directional divergence following an outboard engine failure.
acFhaData.effCrew: Insufficient authority to counter asymmetric thrust.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Total loss of thrust on all four engines
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Forced landing beyond gliding range of a suitable surface.
acFhaData.effCrew: Restart attempts unsuccessful.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of thrust on both engines on the same side
acFhaData.effAc: Large asymmetric moment at low speed; climb gradient not assured at maximum payload.
acFhaData.effCrew: Full rudder and bank required; workload very high.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Undetected thrust asymmetry beyond controllable limits
acFhaData.effAc: Directional divergence before the crew identifies the failed engine.
acFhaData.effCrew: Misidentification of the failed powerplant.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of deceleration capability on a semi-prepared strip
acFhaData.effAc: Overrun beyond the 1,800 m strip onto unprepared ground at maximum payload.
acFhaData.effCrew: No remaining means of deceleration.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of ground directional control
acFhaData.effAc: Departure from a 1,800 m strip with no paved shoulder.
acFhaData.effCrew: Unable to maintain the centreline on a low-friction surface.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of all primary flight display
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Loss of primary attitude reference; standby lane only.
acFhaData.effCrew: Reversion to standby instruments; workload high.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Display of misleading attitude or airspeed without annunciation
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Crew acts on false data; departure from controlled flight.
acFhaData.effCrew: No cue that the data is wrong.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of hazard alerting
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Hazardous states reach the crew late or not at all.
acFhaData.effCrew: Increased workload; reliance on scan.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of ice protection in icing conditions
acFhaData.effAc: Ice accretion on a large, lightly loaded wing; stall margin eroded.
acFhaData.effCrew: Escape maneuver required.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of fuel delivery to all engines
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Total thrust loss; forced landing.
acFhaData.effCrew: Restart unsuccessful.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Landing gear fails to extend or lock
acFhaData.effAc: Gear-up or partial-gear landing on an unpaved surface.
acFhaData.effCrew: Alternate extension attempted; diversion to a paved runway.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Misleading position guidance to an unsurveyed strip
acFhaData.effAc: Approach flown to a surface that is not the intended strip.
acFhaData.effCrew: No independent means to detect the error at low level.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of payload restraint in flight
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: A 72.6 t item moves within a 105 m hold; center of gravity leaves the envelope and structure is overloaded.
acFhaData.effCrew: No means to arrest the movement from the flight deck.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Center of gravity outside the certified envelope at take-off
acFhaData.effAc: Insufficient pitch authority to rotate or to recover after rotation.
acFhaData.effCrew: Control column reaches the stop.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Erroneous weight and balance indication accepted by the crew
acFhaData.effAc: Take-off attempted outside the envelope with no cue that the load sheet is wrong.
acFhaData.effCrew: Crew has no independent check of a single-item load.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of hold pressurization
acFhaData.effAc: Hold reverts to ambient; payload environmental limits may be exceeded.
acFhaData.effCrew: Descent to a lower level required.
acFhaData.effPax: No effect on the flight deck.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Hold over-pressure beyond structural limits
acFhaData.effAc: Rupture of the pressure boundary on a 105 m circular fuselage.
acFhaData.effCrew: No crew action available in the time available.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of flight-deck pressurization and crew oxygen
acFhaData.effAc: Crew incapacitation at 41,000 ft.
acFhaData.effCrew: Time of useful consciousness exceeded before descent.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Nose door unlocks or opens in flight
acFhaData.effAc: Loss of the forward pressure boundary and of primary structure; explosive decompression of the hold.
acFhaData.effCrew: No recovery available.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Loss of nose door lock indication
acFhaData.effAc: Dispatch prevented; no in-flight effect.
acFhaData.effCrew: Door state confirmed by external inspection.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Nose door indicated locked when it is not
acFhaData.effAc: Take-off with an unlocked primary structural door; leads directly to FC-23.
acFhaData.effCrew: Crew has positive but false indication.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Total loss of electrical power
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Loss of flight controls, displays and alerting simultaneously.
acFhaData.effCrew: Battery lane only, for a limited period.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Total loss of hydraulic power
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Loss of primary flight control actuation, braking and steering.
acFhaData.effCrew: No manual reversion on a control surface of this size.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Structural failure resulting from unpaved-surface loads
acFhaData.effAc: Gear or airframe failure from repeated soft-field and irregular-surface loading.
acFhaData.effCrew: No cue before failure.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Undetected or unsuppressed fire in the hold or a nacelle
acFhaData.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
acFhaData.effAc: Fire propagates through a 105 m hold or a pylon before landing.
acFhaData.effCrew: Suppression exhausted or ineffective.

acFhaData.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one engine
acFhaData.effAc: Thrust excursion within the controllable envelope.
acFhaData.effCrew: Crew identifies and shuts down the affected engine.

acReqData.text: The probability of loss of pitch attitude control shall not exceed 1E-9 per flight hour.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification per 14 CFR 25.1309 and AC 25.1309-1B.

acReqData.text: The probability of total loss of thrust from all four powerplants shall not exceed 1E-9 per flight hour.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; four independent powerplants with independent fuel feed.

acReqData.text: The aircraft shall remain controllable and shall meet the applicable climb gradient following the loss of two powerplants on the same side at the most critical point in the take-off.
acReqData.rat: Hazardous classification; four-engine asymmetry case.

acReqData.text: At least two independent means of deceleration shall be available on a semi-prepared surface at maximum landing weight.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; braking coefficient on graded dirt is materially below a paved runway.

acReqData.text: The probability of displaying misleading attitude or airspeed without annunciation shall not exceed 1E-9 per flight hour.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; integrity budget on the display chain.

acReqData.text: The payload restraint system shall retain the maximum payload under the ultimate inertia forces of 14 CFR 25.561 with no single restraint station carrying more than its rated load after any single failure.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; single-item payload occupying the full hold length.

acReqData.text: The probability of take-off with the center of gravity outside the certified envelope shall not exceed 1E-9 per flight hour, including crew and loading procedure error.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; a single 105 m item leaves no averaging effect across the load.

acReqData.text: The probability of erroneous weight and balance indication accepted by the crew during Takeoff shall not exceed 3.00e-9 per flight.
acReqData.rat: FC-19 — Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B. Equivalent to ≤ 1.00e-9 per flight hour averaged over the 3.00 h flight envelope (cert-basis form). Phase: Takeoff. Phase exposure: 0.05 h of 3.15 h flight (r=1.6%; Takeoff). Basic-event allocations under this hazard should be expressed as operational rates during these phases (event-allocation normalization, not target rescaling).

text.from: An independent means, not derived from the load sheet, shall confirm the longitudinal center of gravity before take-off.
text.to: The probability of erroneous weight and balance indication accepted by the crew during Takeoff shall not exceed 3.00e-9 per flight.

rat.from: Removes the single human-error path to a Catastrophic condition.
rat.to: FC-19 — Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B. Equivalent to ≤ 1.00e-9 per flight hour averaged over the 3.00 h flight envelope (cert-basis form). Phase: Takeoff. Phase exposure: 0.05 h of 3.15 h flight (r=1.6%; Takeoff). Basic-event allocations under this hazard should be expressed as operational rates during these phases (event-allocation normalization, not target rescaling).

acReqData.text: The nose cargo door shall be provided with latching, locking and lock-indication functions that are independent of one another, such that no single failure or single crew error can result in take-off with the door unlocked.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; the door is both pressure boundary and primary structure.

acReqData.text: The probability of the nose door being indicated locked when it is not shall not exceed 1E-9 per flight hour.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; false indication defeats the crew check.

acReqData.text: The flight-deck pressure boundary shall be independent of the cargo hold pressure schedule, and crew oxygen shall be available for the time required to descend from 41,000 ft to 10,000 ft.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; the hold is pressurized to a lower schedule than the flight deck.

acReqData.text: Electrical power for the functions required for continued safe flight and landing shall be available from at least two independent sources after any single failure.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification.

acReqData.text: Flight control actuation shall remain available following the loss of any single hydraulic system.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; no manual reversion is credible at this control surface size.

acReqData.text: The landing gear and supporting structure shall withstand the design number of landings on a semi-prepared surface meeting the published strip specification, with damage tolerance demonstrated.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; repeated soft-field loading has no service precedent at this weight.

acReqData.text: Ice protection shall be provided for all surfaces whose contamination affects stall margin or air-data integrity.
acReqData.rat: Hazardous classification.

acReqData.text: Fire detection and suppression shall be provided in each nacelle, the cargo hold and each wheel well, with suppression sufficient for the maximum diversion time.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; 105 m hold with a single-item load.

acReqData.text: Directional control shall be maintained following the failure of the most critical engine at the most critical point in the take-off, with the twin-fin empennage sized accordingly.
acReqData.rat: Catastrophic classification; outboard engine moment arm on an 80 m span.

acReqData.text: Approach guidance to an unsurveyed strip shall include an independent means of confirming that the intended surface has been acquired.
acReqData.rat: Hazardous classification; no published approach exists to a wind-farm strip.

Phase: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing. Phase exposure: 2.50 h of 3.15 h flight (r=79.4%; Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing). acReqData.text: Wheel braking, Reverse thrust unavailable on all powerplants, and Lift dump shall be functionally independent.
acReqData.rat: Derived by AND-family gate G-7149 (Loss of deceleration capability on landing) of the allocation tree per ARP 4754A §5.4.1: the gate's budget split assumes no common cause couples its members, so they must be functionally independent (no shared function, signal, software or development error); physical independence is a companion requirement. Children: G-7138 (Wheel braking lost), G-7145 (Reverse thrust unavailable on all powerplants), G-7148 (Lift dump unavailable). DAL reduction withheld: independence is claimed but not yet substantiated, and CMA substantiation (ARP4761A App M) is REQUIRED before the reduction can be taken.

snapshot.rat: ARP4754B §5.1.8 — a human-performed task relied on to ensure safety is to be identified and recorded in the certification data; §5.3.1.4 is the class it is recorded as. §5.3.1.4 defines operational requirements as the interface between the flight crew and the functional system; the declared sensory channels ARE that interface. The assumption also declares cognitive — those describe what the crew does with the information, not what the system must present, so they are deliberately not requirements here. acAssumptionsData.text: The flight crew recognizes and reacts to an annunciated pitch or display failure within 3 seconds in the approach configuration.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Simulator campaign to be run on the flight-deck mock-up.

acAssumptionsData.text: [SPEC] Four engines are podded on pylons beneath a high wing. The outboard engine moment arm is taken as 0.35 of the 80 m semi-span.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Confirm the engine spanwise stations against the released configuration drawing.

acAssumptionsData.text: [SPEC] The powerplants are an existing certified turbofan model. The type has been selected but is not yet released to the safety team, so a mature in-production engine IFSD rate is assumed.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Replace with the selected engine type and its service data once released.

acAssumptionsData.text: [SPEC] The landing distance requirement is 1,800 m / 6,000 ft on a semi-prepared surface. Landing rollout is predicted at approximately 1,080 m.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Aircraft specification, top-level requirement.

acAssumptionsData.text: The braking coefficient available on a graded dirt or gravel strip is taken as 0.35 of the dry paved value, and is degraded further when wet.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Requires substantiation against the strip specification, which is not yet defined.

acAssumptionsData.text: Air data and attitude are sourced from three independent channels with a voting monitor.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: No avionics architecture has been released; confirm with the systems group.

acAssumptionsData.text: The icing envelope is 14 CFR Part 25 Appendix C. Appendix O has not been assumed.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Confirm the intended icing certification scope.

acAssumptionsData.text: Approaches are flown to unsurveyed strips at the wind-farm perimeter with no published instrument procedure.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Derived from the stated operating concept; confirm minima and approach aids.

acAssumptionsData.text: [SPEC] The design payload case is a single 105 m blade of up to 72.6 t occupying the full hold length; alternatives are two 95 m or three 80 m blades.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Aircraft specification, top-level requirement.

acAssumptionsData.text: The payload is restrained at discrete stations along the hold. Neither the restraint architecture nor its rated loads are yet defined; a station spacing of 6 m with dual load paths per station is assumed.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Replace with the actual restraint design.

acAssumptionsData.text: Weight and balance for a single-item load is established from the item certificate and loading position, with no independent on-aircraft measurement assumed.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: This assumption drives REQ-AC-008; if an on-board weighing system exists, the requirement changes.

acAssumptionsData.text: [PRELIM] The hold is pressurized to a low differential, currently sized to roughly 8,800 m hold altitude, on a circular fuselage cross-section. The differential is not frozen and is assumed at 3.5 psi.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Confirm the pressure schedule and relief settings.

acAssumptionsData.text: The flight deck is on a separate, higher pressure schedule from the hold, with independent supply and crew oxygen.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Nothing in the released data defines the flight-deck pressure boundary. This is the assumption most likely to be wrong.

acAssumptionsData.text: [SPEC] Loading is through an upward-hinging nose cargo door, following established outsized-freighter practice.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Aircraft specification, loading concept.

acAssumptionsData.text: The nose door latching, locking and indication functions are assumed independent. Nothing released describes them.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: This is the assumption behind REQ-AC-009 and REQ-AC-010; both fall if it is wrong.

acAssumptionsData.text: Electrical generation is assumed as one generator per engine plus an APU generator, with a battery lane for essential loads.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: No electrical architecture has been released.

acAssumptionsData.text: Three independent hydraulic systems are assumed, in the manner of comparable four-engine transports.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: No hydraulic architecture has been released.

acAssumptionsData.text: [PRELIM] Twenty tires spread the footprint pressure, with tire sizing derived from a tactical airlifter. The number of gear legs and bogies is not frozen and is assumed as one nose unit and four main bogies.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Confirm the gear arrangement with the landing-system supplier.

acAssumptionsData.text: The cargo hold is assumed to be a Class E compartment in the manner of a large freighter, with detection and depressurization rather than active suppression.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Confirm the intended compartment classification; a 105 m hold has no direct precedent.

acAssumptionsData.text: The certification basis is assumed to be 14 CFR Part 25 with special conditions for size, the nose door, the payload restraint and semi-prepared operation. No certification basis has yet been agreed with the authority.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: This is the single largest open item. The program has an FAA pathway and a named regulatory lead, but no agreed basis, amendment level or special conditions.

acAssumptionsData.text: The loading crew verifies restraint tension at every station before the nose door is closed.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Task analysis and observed loading trial.

acAssumptionsData.text: The flight crew confirms nose door lock state from two independent indications before take-off.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Procedure design and simulator validation.

acAssumptionsData.text: The flight crew detects and responds to a thrust asymmetry on a four-engine aircraft within 2 seconds during take-off.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Simulator campaign; four-engine asymmetry is harder to identify than a twin.

acAssumptionsData.text: The flight crew maintains the centreline on a dust-limited approach to an unlit strip without external visual cues below 100 ft.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Simulator campaign with a brownout model; may drive a requirement for additional guidance.

acAssumptionsData.text: The load sheet for a single-item payload is independently checked by a second person before departure.
acAssumptionsData.valStrategy: Procedure design; this is the only barrier to FC-19 until REQ-AC-008 is implemented.

req.text: The probability of loss of all generated electrical power during Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing shall not exceed 3.00e-9 per flight.
req.rat: FC-EPS01 — Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B. Equivalent to ≤ 1.00e-9 per flight hour averaged over the 3.00 h flight envelope (cert-basis form). Phase: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing. Phase exposure: 2.50 h of 3.15 h flight (r=79.4%; Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing). Basic-event allocations under this hazard should be expressed as operational rates during these phases (event-allocation normalization, not target rescaling).

praData.desc: High-energy debris across four rotor-burst planes rather than two
praData.systems: Propulsion, Fuel System, Hydraulic Power System, Electrical Power System
praData.csfl: An inboard burst plane crosses the center wing box where the fuel gallery and two hydraulic systems converge
praData.mitigation: Feed and hydraulic separation outside the ±15° burst plane; gallery shielding; retention requirement carried forward

praData.threat: Debris ingestion and impact from a semi-prepared surface
praData.desc: Stones, dust and organic debris thrown by twenty tires on graded dirt
praData.systems: Propulsion, Landing Gear & Braking, Ice Protection System
praData.csfl: Simultaneous damage to more than two powerplants during a single take-off roll
praData.mitigation: High-wing podded installation raises the intakes; debris deflectors; strip specification limits loose material

praData.desc: Burst of one of twenty tires at high energy on an unpaved surface
praData.systems: Landing Gear & Braking, Hydraulic Power System, Fuel System
praData.csfl: Tire debris severing both brake supply lines in the wheel well
praData.mitigation: Line separation and shielding in the burst zone; see CMA-003

praData.desc: A 72.6 t item moving within a 105 m hold
praData.systems: Cargo Handling & Restraint, Flight Control System
praData.csfl: Longitudinal movement takes the center of gravity outside the envelope and overloads the hold floor
praData.mitigation: Dual load paths per station; tension monitoring; loading procedure constraints

praData.desc: Loss of a door that is both pressure boundary and primary structure
praData.systems: Nose Cargo Door, Environmental Control & Pressurization
praData.csfl: Latch, lock and indication defeated by a single hinge-line event
praData.mitigation: Separate latch and lock mechanisms; two independent lock sensing channels; take-off configuration inhibit

praData.desc: Impact on the nose, the leading edges and four intakes
praData.systems: Propulsion, Avionics & Display, Flight Control System
praData.csfl: A flocking-bird encounter affecting more than two powerplants on approach
praData.mitigation: Intake separation across the span; nose structure qualified to the applicable Part 25 threat

praData.desc: Attachment across an 80 m span and a 109 m fuselage
praData.systems: Electrical Power System, Avionics & Display, Fuel System
praData.csfl: Attachment at a composite wing joint adjacent to a fuel tank boundary
praData.mitigation: Bonding and lightning protection at the aluminum-to-composite joints; fuel tank ignition prevention

praData.desc: Fire in a 105 m compartment with a single-item load
praData.csfl: Detection delay across the hold length exceeds the time to diversion
praData.mitigation: Dual detection loops per hold third; compartment classification and diversion planning

praData.desc: Rapid loss of the low-differential hold pressure
praData.systems: Environmental Control & Pressurization, Cargo Handling & Restraint
praData.csfl: Decompression loads on the flight-deck floor, which is the boundary between two pressure schedules
praData.mitigation: Blow-out panels; flight-deck boundary qualified for the differential collapse case

praData.desc: Gust response of a very large, lightly loaded airframe at Mach 0.6
praData.systems: Flight Control System, Cargo Handling & Restraint
praData.csfl: Gust load exceeding the restraint rating with a single long item
praData.mitigation: Turbulence penetration procedure; restraint rating margin substantiated against the gust spectrum

praData.threat: Brownout and dust ingestion on landing
praData.desc: Loss of visual reference and abrasive ingestion on a dry graded strip
praData.csfl: Loss of visual reference at the flare with no approach lighting available
praData.mitigation: Independent position confirmation; crew procedure for a dust-limited approach

praData.threat: Wheel-well fire after a rejected take-off
praData.desc: Brake energy on an unpaved surface with limited cooling airflow
praData.systems: Landing Gear & Braking, Fire Protection, Hydraulic Power System
praData.csfl: Fire in a wheel well containing both brake hydraulic supplies
praData.mitigation: Brake energy limits and cooling schedule; wheel-well detection

praData.threat: Fuel tank or fuel line leakage
praData.desc: Escape of fuel from a tank boundary, coupling or transfer line into an adjacent zone.
praData.systems: Fuel System, Electrical Power System, Propulsion
praData.csfl: Flammable fluid reaching a compartment whose ignition sources and drainage were never assessed against it
praData.mitigation: Flammable-fluid leakage zones declared and drained; ignition sources kept out of the envelope; keel-beam runs shrouded where they pass the gallery

praData.threat: Battery leakage, fire or thermal runaway
praData.desc: A cell vents or enters self-sustaining thermal runaway, propagating through the pack and releasing gas at pressure.
praData.csfl: Fire adjacent to the crew oxygen distribution run, with an event that carries its own oxidiser
praData.mitigation: Pack-level non-propagation demonstrated; overboard venting with the vent path assessed as a zone; oxygen run rerouted outboard

praData.threat: Ram air turbine burst or uncommanded deployment
praData.desc: Blade or hub liberation from the deployed RAT, or deployment at a speed the deployed configuration is not cleared for.
praData.systems: Electrical Power System, Hydraulic Power System
praData.csfl: Debris through the aft fuselage, or a structural load case at an uncleared speed
praData.mitigation: Deployed-RAT debris envelope applied to the surrounding zone; uplock shown single-failure and vibration tolerant; deployed-configuration speed limitation published

praData.desc: Failure of a bleed duct releasing gas at engine delivery temperature and pressure into the surrounding compartment.
praData.systems: Environmental Control & Pressurization, Ice Protection System, Propulsion
praData.csfl: Jet impingement and sustained heating on equipment and wiring qualified for a far lower environment
praData.mitigation: Compartment relief sized for the burst case; impingement envelope cleared of flight-critical runs; overheat detection independent of the ruptured duct

praData.threat: Wheel flange or hub fragment release
praData.desc: Liberation of a metallic wheel flange or hub fragment on a trajectory set by the wheel plane, distinct from tire burst and tread flail.
praData.systems: Landing Gear & Braking, Hydraulic Power System
praData.csfl: Gear bay contents and both brake supplies inside a single wheel plane
praData.mitigation: Wheel-plane fragment envelope applied alongside the tire-burst envelope; redundant pairs kept out of a single plane; fuse-plug behavior demonstrated

praData.desc: Rupture or leakage of a pressurized or hazardous-fluid container carried in the type design or as cargo.
praData.systems: Crew Oxygen, Fire Protection, Cargo Handling & Restraint
praData.csfl: A chemical and pressure environment in a compartment assessed for neither, with occupant exposure governing
praData.mitigation: Every pressurized container in the type design identified and its release assessed into the containing compartment; dangerous-goods loading limits published

praData.desc: Failure of the pressure boundary between the pressurized hold and the unpressurised tail cone.
praData.systems: Environmental Control & Pressurization, Flight Control System
praData.csfl: Decompression plus a differential load case on surrounding structure and on the fin actuation runs crossing the boundary
praData.mitigation: Boundary demonstrated against the rupture case; actuation runs shown to survive the release path; floor and partition venting sized for the compartment differential

cmaData.subject: Elevator actuation lane dissimilarity
cmaData.claim: Lanes A and B fail independently (option-1 claim on the pitch AND gate).
cmaData.findings: Different suppliers and technologies assumed. A common installation torque procedure would defeat the claim.
cmaData.mitigation: Separate installation task cards; β = 5% residual commonality retained in the quantitative model.

cmaData.subject: Four-engine independence
cmaData.claim: No single event takes more than two powerplants.
cmaData.findings: The dominant threats are a common maintenance error across a line-maintenance visit and debris ingestion on a semi-prepared strip, which is a genuinely common cause across all four intakes.
cmaData.mitigation: Staggered maintenance intervals across engine positions; strip specification limits loose material; PRA-002 carries the residual.

cmaData.subject: Brake supply independence
cmaData.claim: Hydraulic systems A and B brake supplies fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Both runs share the main wheel well, which is also the tire-burst zone (PRA-003) and the wheel-well fire zone (PRA-012).
cmaData.mitigation: 400 mm separation with an intervening firewall; residual commonality retained.

cmaData.subject: Hydraulic system separation at the wing root
cmaData.claim: Systems A and B are independent.
cmaData.findings: Both converge in Z-CWB alongside the fuel gallery, inside an inboard rotor-burst plane.
cmaData.mitigation: Routing revised outside the burst plane; requirement 2132 raised and open.

cmaData.subject: Twin-fin rudder independence
cmaData.claim: Left and right rudder actuation fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Both control runs pass through the horizontal stabiliser torque box, which is a single structural element joining the two fins.
cmaData.mitigation: Opposite-side routing within the box; structural failure of the box is treated as a separate structural case, not a systems independence claim.

cmaData.subject: Nose door lock indication independence
cmaData.findings: Both channels are assumed to pass through the same hinge-line penetration, which defeats the claim outright. This is the most consequential open finding in the model.
cmaData.mitigation: Split the penetration and separate the harness routes; until then the FC-25 budget is not met.

cmaData.subject: Electrical generation independence
cmaData.findings: Identical generator part numbers across four positions create a design-error common mode.
cmaData.mitigation: Dissimilar control units; staggered overhaul; β = 3% retained.

cmaData.subject: Air-data channel independence
cmaData.claim: Three air-data channels fail independently in the erroneous sense.
cmaData.findings: Common icing of multiple pitot sources is a recognized environmental common mode; probe heating independence is the mitigation.
cmaData.mitigation: Independently powered and monitored heaters per probe (requirement 2171).

cmaData.subject: Powerplant unit independence (min 2 of 4)
cmaData.claim: The four powerplants fail independently, so the min-2-of-4 configuration holds.
cmaData.findings: All four are the same type from the same production lot, serviced on the same visit by the same crew, and the inboard pair sits inside the outboard pair’s rotor-burst plane.
cmaData.mitigation: Staggered maintenance across the wing; burst-plane segregation applied to the fuel and control runs; a manufacturing-lot commonality factor retained in the quantitative model.

cmaData.subject: Hydraulic system independence (min 2 of 3)
cmaData.claim: Systems A, B and C fail independently, so any two carry flight-control actuation.
cmaData.findings: B and C share the keel beam over a long continuous run in Z-BELLY, which exceeds the 3 m separation limit in requirement 2132.
cmaData.mitigation: Routing revision proposed; until it is applied the min-2-of-3 claim is not substantiated for a keel-beam event.

cmaData.subject: Thrust asymmetry annunciation independence
cmaData.claim: The asymmetry annunciation is independent of the powerplant control that causes the asymmetry.
cmaData.findings: Annunciation is derived from the same engine control channel that commands thrust, so a channel error can produce an asymmetry and suppress its own annunciation.
cmaData.mitigation: Cross-channel comparison against the opposite-side engine proposed; the min-3-of-4 asymmetry clause is unsubstantiated until it is in.

cmaData.subject: Single-member configuration claims
cmaData.claim: Where a MAC clause names one system, no further redundancy is required for the protected function.
cmaData.findings: Twelve clauses are single-member. Each is a claim that a single zonal event taking that system is acceptable, and the spatial model currently returns twenty-eight such paths to a Catastrophic condition.
cmaData.mitigation: Each path to be dispositioned individually on the zonal desk with a signed engineering basis, or the architecture revised. Four are signed; the rest are open.

cmaData.subject: Bleed-duct routing against redundant channels
cmaData.claim: A high-pressure duct rupture does not defeat any redundant pair.
cmaData.findings: The impingement envelope from the inboard pylon ducts has not yet been applied to the hydraulic runs in Z-CWB.
cmaData.mitigation: Impingement analysis raised against PRA-016; overheat detection independent of the ruptured duct required.

cmaData.subject: Maintenance-error commonality across the nose-door latch set
cmaData.claim: A maintenance error does not affect more than one latch.
cmaData.findings: All four latches are rigged in one task by one technician against one datum.
cmaData.mitigation: Independent post-rig verification by a second technician, and a lock-state check at the first pressurization.

tasks.name: Nose door lock rigging and lock-sensor check

problemReports.title: Nose door lock proximity sensor intermittent below -30 °C
problemReports.description: Cold-soak rig: one of the four lock sensors reported unlocked-then-locked within 200 ms during a cold cycle.
problemReports.disposition: Sensor gap tolerance tightened (ECN-0207); 60 cold cycles clean.

history.note: gap tolerance at the cold end of the band

problemReports.title: Restraint tension readings drift between load sheet and rig
problemReports.description: Tension values recorded by the loading crew differ from rig instrumentation by up to 12% on the aft stations.

deferral.rationale: Bounded by the pre-departure re-tension check; instrumented loading trial scheduled with the second airframe.

history.note: signed deferral to the second airframe

problemReports.title: Hold pressurization outflow valve authority lower than modeled
problemReports.description: Valve supplier data shows less authority at the top of the envelope than the pressurization model assumes.

history.note: model updated; requirement impact under review

problemReports.title: Brake accumulator pre-charge loss on the second airframe
problemReports.description: Pre-charge found below limit at two consecutive checks with no fault annunciated.
problemReports.disposition: Accumulator replaced; pre-charge check added to the walk-around.

history.note: closed at the review; signature not captured

problemReports.title: Ice protection controller reset observed during a generator transfer
problemReports.description: Controller reset once during a channel transfer on the ground rig; protection restored in under two seconds.

history.note: held pending the B2 controller drop

ZSA:ins.rationale: No aircraft exists. The zonal analysis is a desktop review against the released configuration and is recorded as ZSA rev A, demonstration only.

safetyProgramPlan.notes: Demonstration project. The HL-1 is a fictional aircraft — see the assumption register for what the specification gave us and what we assumed.

intake.basis: ASSUMED 14 CFR Part 25 / AC 25.1309-1B — no certification basis has yet been agreed

zone:Z-MLGW|FC-28.basis: Unpaved-surface load case is carried by the structural substantiation, not by gear redundancy — PRA-006 and the semi-prepared strip spec. Gear bay contents are not in the load path.

zone:Z-NLGW|FC-28.basis: As Z-MLGW: the unpaved load case is structural. Nose bay contents do not carry the airframe load path.

zone:Z-EMP|FC-04.basis: Twin-fin rudder installation: the two fins are structurally separated by the full span of the horizontal stabiliser, and no single credible zonal event envelops both. Retained against CMA-005.

zone:Z-NZDR|FC-25.basis: Lock indication is proved by a direct-drive proximity set on each of the four latches, powered from the opposite electrical channel to the latch actuation. Residual risk carried by the pre-departure lock check in the AFM.

reviewCommentsData.text: Classification challenged. FC-19 is carried Catastrophic on the assumption that the crew accepts an erroneous load sheet without an independent check. If the second-crew verification in ASM-HL-014 holds, this is Hazardous — and if it does not, the assumption is doing the work the requirement should be doing. Needs closing before baseline.

The unpaved-surface load case cites the semi-prepared strip spec, but the spec was revised to a lower CBR after this row was written. Re-run the load case against the current figure before this is signed again.

This tree apportions the whole budget to the loading process and models no detection. There is a weight-and-balance cross-check in the flight-deck load sheet — either it earns credit here or we should say why it does not.
Verification evidence predates ECN-0142. The analysis report referenced here was issued against the pre-change restraint layout, so the Passed state is not supported by current evidence.
The β = 5% residual commonality is asserted, not derived. Independence on this gate is the basis of an option-1 DAL claim, so the number needs a source before the claim stands.
Latch proximity sensing and the lock indication share a harness run through Z-NZDR. That is a common-cause path against the independence this row assumes.
Hold over-pressure was reclassified when the outflow valve authority changed. Raised here so the trail shows why, and resolved once the revised valve schedule was accepted.
reviewCommentsData.resolutionNote: Accepted — the aft-limit case is bounded by the loading procedure revision.

rules.containment: A part is in the zone whose volume holds its centroid. The deepest zone wins; at equal depth the smaller volume, then the lower zone code, then the lower id, and the part is reported as ambiguous. A part whose box crosses the boundary of its zone is reported as straddling.
rules.identity: A link is to one installed copy, never to a part number. Only a reference designator (the installed item tag) that is unique on both sides, one CAD part and one equipment item, links by itself. A shared part number or an ATA code is only a candidate, because the same part can be installed several times doing different jobs. Every candidate waits for the engineer to confirm. Equipment is never placed in a zone without a confirmed link.
rules.events: A basic event belongs to the equipment its declared identity names (the system id, or the provider of an interface or resource event).
rules.impact: Every basic event of the affected equipment is failed together, everything else works, and each fault tree is evaluated by the existing engine. A failure condition is reached when one of its trees needs no further failure.
rules.independence: An AND gate derives a physical and functional independence requirement. Equipment under two different inputs of an AND, priority AND, spare, sequence or k-of-n (k of 2 or more) gate in the same zone is a violation; in nested zones or in sibling zones with no substantiated barrier between them, an advisory; inside the same particular-risk volume, a violation; the same equipment under two inputs, a violation.
rules.riskVolume: A part is inside a particular-risk volume when any of 27 points of its box (corners, edge midpoints, face centers, center) is inside the volume.
